messages:
sarah: Hey team — I opened a PR to refresh the onboarding runbook for new engineers. Main goals: simplify the hello-world app flow, tighten the auth example (token vs API key), and make first deployment steps explicit. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2345 :wave:

riyad: skimmed the PR — overall looks good. Two quick asks: 1) the JS SDK example still uses .createSession() which is deprecated, switch to client.generate() 2) add note about TOKEN expiry for dev keys.

elaine: +1 on the session rename. Also the curl snippet has a hardcoded bearer token in the example — let's replace with $REDWOOD_API_KEY and an example of how to export it.

kevin: small nit on the deployment section: we say "deploy to dedicated" but don't show region/instance sizing. Can we add a minimal example: GPU vs CPU quick guidance? even one sentence is fine.

sarah: Good catches. I'll update JS snippet and the curl vars. For the token expiry — do we have a canonical line? riyad?

riyad: use: "export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-<short-example> (dev keys expire after 30d). For long-term use, point to the Console -> API keys -> Create service key (no expiry)." Put that in a callout.

sam: I can fix the python SDK snippet today. Current example mixes sync/async patterns. Will standardize to async with an await example and minimal error handling.

elaine: For the hello-world app, can we keep the minimal code under 20 lines? New hires skip over giant blocks. Maybe link to a full example repo instead of inlining everything.

kevin: Agree. Inline minimal snippet + "See full starter repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/starter-apps/tree/main/hello-world"

docs-bot: lint check queued for PR #2345 — running markdown link validator and code snippet linter. Results in ~5m. :robot_face:

riyad: One more: in the "first deployment" section we call out `--no-wait` flag in the example deploy command, which hides errors during CI. Suggest remove it or add a note: "use only during iterative dev".

sarah: Good point. I'll remove it and add a paragraph about recommended CI flags. Also adding a tiny checklist at top: prerequisites (node, python, export API key, git), expected time to finish (10-15m).

sam: pushed a commit to the PR branch to fix python snippet (force-pushed branch sam/compact-python). Also added a one-liner about token rotation best practices.

elaine: ran the examples locally — the JS snippet had a missing await on stream handler, I filed a tiny inline patch in the PR. All examples now run except the mac path in deploy where dockerfile expects root. I'll add a note about file permissions.

docs-bot: lint checks complete — markdown link validator: OK, code snippet linter: 2 warnings (python -> unused import, js -> console.log left in example). See CI output: https://ci.internal.redwood/2345.

kevin: once those two warnings are fixed, I'm happy to approve. Also would like a short blurb about Dedicated vs Hosted in onboarding so folks understand when to choose which. (2-3 sentences)

sarah: I'll add that blurb and fix the console.log. Plan: update PR by EOD, request final reviews, then merge after CI passes. If anyone wants to pair on wording for the Dedicated vs Hosted blurb, ping me. :thumbsup:

riyad: quick QA: can we add one-line command for verifying auth after export? e.g., `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` returns 200. That helps new hires verify env.

sarah: Perfect — adding that health-check command now.

sam: updated PR. PTAL.

kevin: looked at latest diff — LGTM from me. :shipit:

elaine: approved. :white_check_mark:

riyad: approved after the blurb tweak to mention "service keys" vs "interactive keys". Done.

docs-bot: PR #2345 merged into main by sarah — deploy job queued. Release note: docs: onboarding runbook refresh (auth, examples, first-deploy)

sarah: thanks everyone! I'll follow up if anything pops during the deploy. We should schedule a tiny post-merge doc-check in #docs next week to catch any leftover wording issues. :coffee:
